QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_89

question.text: A stock trades at Rs. 800 in the spot market. The 2-month futures are at Rs. 805. The fair value of futures (including cost of carry) is Rs. 815. What arbitrage should a trader execute?

answer.text: Reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage: Sell (short) the stock at Rs. 800 and simultaneously buy the futures at Rs. 805, earning the Rs. 10 mispricing
Cash-and-carry arbitrage: Buy the stock at Rs. 800 and sell the futures at Rs. 805
No arbitrage is possible because futures are still above spot price
Wait for the futures to reach Rs. 815 before executing any strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step analysis: 1. Fair futures value = Rs. 815 2. Actual futures price = Rs. 805 3. Actual futures of Rs. 805 are below fair value of Rs. 815 by Rs. 10, so futures are underpriced. Reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage: - Short sell the stock at Rs. 800 and invest the proceeds - Buy futures at Rs. 805 - At expiry: take delivery via futures at Rs. 805 and return the stock - Profit captures the Rs. 10 mispricing between actual futures and fair value, net of carry adjustments The Trap: Cash-and-carry is for overpriced futures (futures above fair value), not for the present case. The fact that futures are above spot does not mean they are overpriced; the comparison must be with fair value. Waiting serves no purpose for an arbitrageur. Note: Pages 44, 56, and 95 of the Series VIII workbook support reverse cash-and-carry as long futures plus short cash/underlying when futures are below fair/theoretical price.
